title: Quiz: What AI is, and what it isn't

questions.question: A collar flags a cow whose chewing time has dropped. Which kind of AI is that?

answers.text: AI that senses
answers.feedback: Right. It reads movement and chewing, learns what's normal for that cow, and flags a change.

answers.text: AI that writes and talks
answers.feedback: Chat tools write and talk. The collar doesn't write anything; it reads the cow's activity.

answers.text: AI that predicts the weather
answers.feedback: Weather models predict. The collar is reading the cow's own pattern.

answers.text: It isn't AI at all
answers.feedback: Learning what's normal for each cow and flagging changes is a sensing kind of AI.

questions.feedback: Collars, cameras and scales that read the world and spot patterns are AI that senses.

questions.question: How does a chat AI like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude or Copilot come up with an answer?

answers.text: It looks the answer up in a checked database of facts
answers.feedback: It doesn't. It writes from patterns in what it has read, which is why it can be wrong.

answers.text: It picks likely next words, one after another, from patterns in what it has read
answers.feedback: Right. That's why its answers read well, and why a likely-sounding answer isn't always true.

answers.text: A person reads your question and types the reply
answers.feedback: No person is involved in writing the answer.

answers.text: It measures things on your farm through your phone
answers.feedback: It knows nothing about your farm unless you tell it or give it data.

questions.feedback: A chat AI predicts likely words. Likely isn't the same as true.

questions.question: Which of these is a good job to give a chat AI?

answers.text: Turning your notes from the stock agent's call into a tidy summary
answers.feedback: Right. You supply the facts, it does the writing, and you can check it against your notes.

answers.text: Telling you this week's schedule price for prime lambs
answers.feedback: It can give an old or overseas price with full confidence. Get prices from your processor or agent.

answers.text: Telling you how much rain fell on your farm last month, with nothing attached
answers.feedback: Without your data it can only guess, as the build showed.

answers.text: Deciding whether a sick ewe needs the vet
answers.feedback: That's a call for you and your vet, not a chat tool.

questions.feedback: Chat AI does best when you give it the facts and ask it to work with them.

questions.question: Which of these are ways a chat AI commonly gets things wrong? Pick all that apply.

answers.text: Inventing facts and stating them with confidence
answers.feedback: Yes. These are often called hallucinations.

answers.text: Giving out-of-date information
answers.feedback: Yes. It learned from text gathered up to a point in time.

answers.text: Guessing about your farm when you haven't told it anything
answers.feedback: Yes. It fills the gaps with what's typical, which may be nothing like your place.

answers.text: Refusing to answer any question about farming
answers.feedback: It will happily answer farming questions. The risk is that it answers when it doesn't know.

questions.feedback: Made-up facts, out-of-date knowledge and guesses about your farm are the big three.

questions.question: An AI answer sounds very sure of itself. What does that tell you about whether it's right?

answers.text: It's very likely right
answers.feedback: It sounds just as sure when it's guessing. Tone tells you nothing.

answers.text: Nothing. You judge it by what you can check, such as a source or your own records
answers.feedback: Right. Check the facts, not the tone.

answers.text: It has checked its answer on the internet
answers.feedback: Not necessarily. Many answers come from patterns, not a search.

answers.text: It's wrong, because real experts hedge
answers.feedback: Confident answers can be right too. You still can't tell from the tone.

questions.feedback: A confident tone tells you nothing about accuracy.

questions.question: You've been asking about shearing. Now you want help with a calf rearing plan. What should you do?

answers.text: Keep going in the same chat so it remembers everything
answers.feedback: Earlier talk about shearing can creep into the calf answers.

answers.text: Start a fresh chat
answers.feedback: Right. A new topic gets a clean start, so the old chat doesn't steer the answer.

answers.text: Close the app and wait a day
answers.feedback: No need to wait. Just start a new chat.

answers.text: Type the question in capitals so it knows it's new
answers.feedback: Capitals don't change anything. A fresh chat does.

questions.feedback: Start a fresh chat when you change topic.

questions.question: In the build, you asked about rain since 1 July with no data, then with your rain card. What's the main lesson?

answers.text: AI is useless for farm questions
answers.feedback: With the card it could reason from real numbers. The data made the difference.

answers.text: AI without your data guesses. AI with your data can reason
answers.feedback: Right. Every later module adds more of your farm's own data.

answers.text: The first answer is always right if it sounds sure
answers.feedback: The cold answer often sounds just as sure, and can be well off.

answers.text: Rain gauges and climate grid cells always agree
answers.feedback: They measure different things: one spot versus a ~25 km cell. That's why the card shows both.

questions.feedback: AI without your data guesses. AI with your data can reason.
